headline: Finance Committee to award bids for a pickup truck, a trailer, lead abatement at 6 Davis Street, and a water meter purchase waiver.
summary: The committee will vote on recommendations to award bid 2026-054 for a 1-Ton 4X4 pickup, bid 2026-055 for an enclosed contractor trailer, and bid 2026-056 for lead abatement at 6 Davis Street. It will also consider authorizing a Waiver of Competition for an EJ Prescott water main replacement purchase and discuss Payment in Lieu of Taxes.
items: Recommendation to award bid 2026-054 One (1) 1-Ton 4X4 Pickup
Recommendation to award bid 2026-055 Enclosed Contractor Trailer
Recommendation to award bid 2026-056 Lead Abatement of 6 Davis Street

Other Business: Payment in Lieu of Taxes

Subject: Bid 2026-056 Lead Abatement 6 Davis Street 
Date: October 19, 2026 
 
As part of the $7,000,000 Lead Hazard and $750,000 Supplement Healthy Home HUD grant, Economic 
Development took in -house the task of bidding lead abatement projects for owners eligible under the 
grant to better comply with federal procurement regulations. As a result, Development has a third-party 
responsibility of hiring a lead contractor for the owner under the terms of the grant. 
 
Community Concepts prepared the bid specifications for bid 2026-056 Lead Abatement 6 Davis Street. 
 
The Lead grant considers 6 Davis Street a three (3) unit program-qualifying building.  There is adequate 
available Lead grant funding for the project.  The CDBG rehab program is providing  the $4,500 owner 
lead grant match (max of $40,000 per eligible unit and $1,500 per unit owner match).   
 
Bids were solicited from the four teen (14) licensed  lead abatement contractor s; six (6) attended the 
required mandatory pre-bid meeting, and six (6) were received. The Assistant Community Development 
Manager reviewed the proposals.  A copy of the recommendation is attached.  
 
It is recommended that bid 2026-056 for the Lead Abatement of 6 Davis Street be awarded to Renovate 
Right, Wales, ME, at their bid price of $ 60,365, including the rehab program-provided $4,500 owner 
match. 
 
There is adequate funding for the project in the sources identified with the owner match (519-500001 and 
519-500005).

Item #6                                                                            
 
To: Finance Committee 
From Allen Ward, Deputy Director of Budgeting and Purchasing  
Subject: Waiver of Competition Kamstrup Water Meter Swap-out Purchase 
Date: October 19, 2026 
 
Staff is requesting a Waiver of Competition under Section 3.3.1 of the City’s Purchasing Policy , 
specifically item #7, as follows for consideration:  
 
8.) A contract is already in place, and it is appropriate for the current vendor to provide additional services 
for a specific project that is an extension of the original scope previously approved within the purchasing 
policy. 
 
Doing so will allow the Water Division to contract with EJ Prescott to implement swapping out Lewiston’s 
9,279 water meters .  Under the terms of the contract, Lewiston Water and Sewer Division agrees to 
purchase all water works services, products , and materials used in its service area from EJP.  As such, 
Lewiston would be moving toward the installation of Kamstrup water meters given EJP’s ending its 
relationship with Sensus/Xylem meters. The City Administrator has approved consideration for the Public 
Works Director’s proposal, saving Lewiston significant lease interest costs.    
 
The Public Works Director recommends t he City Council’s allocated $500,000 FY27 Water and Sewer 
operating budget  go toward s the installation of a meter reading antenna and replacement of as many 
Kamstrup meters as funding allows. In addition, the department will include a $3.75million Water and 
Sewer Capital Improvement request to fund purchasing the remaining Kamstrup water meters.  
 
It is recommended to authorize a Waiver of Competition to accept EJ Prescott’s proposal to switch to the  
Kamstrup metering program, including leak detection services.  
 
There is adequate funding in the source identified for th e year one, FY27 meter replacements  in the 
Deputy Public Works Director’s memo (6085-640301, 6250-662509).

SUBJECT:  Waiver of Competition for Kamstrup Metering Program  
 
Public Works is requesting a Waiver of Competition for the procurement of a new water 
metering system through E.J. Prescott (EJP) for Kamstrup water meters. The 
agreement includes switching out over 9,000 water meters currently in place with new 
smart meter devices. It also includes leak detection to help prevent water main breaks 
and to assist customers with managing their usage, a customer portal, and instant water 
meter readings. Please see attached memo from Public Works Director, Kevin Gagne, 
for further details.  
 
Public Works is requesting approval of this Waiver of Competition to install a new water 
metering system for customers in the City through E.J. Prescott (EJP).
